title: Conservation of Energy and Efficiency
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Conservation of Energy and Efficiency Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Apply the law of conservation of energy to analyse system efficiency in terms of energy inputs, outputs, transfers and transformations (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on conservation of energy and efficiency: energy inputs and outputs, Sankey diagrams, efficiency and power calculations, and reducing energy waste. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ energy in × 100%, and it is always less than 100%.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is conserved in every system.

  • Total energy in = useful energy out + wasted energy. Wasted energy is usually heat and sound, not destroyed.
  • Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ total energy in × 100%. No real device reaches 100%.
  • A Sankey diagram shows the split: the width of each arrow is in proportion to the energy.
Example

1000 J in, 250 J useful. Wasted? Efficiency?

1000 − 250 = 750 J

250 ÷ 1000 × 100

Answer: 750 J wasted, 25%

Example

A car engine: input? useful? wasted?

chemical energy in petrol

Answer: kinetic useful; heat and sound wasted

Common mistakes

  • Giving useful + wasted energy that adds to more than the input.
  • Calculating an efficiency over 100%.
  • Saying wasted energy is 'destroyed' or 'used up'.

faq.a: A flow diagram that shows how input energy splits into useful and wasted outputs. The arrow widths are drawn in proportion to the amounts of energy.
Friction, electrical resistance and sound always transfer some energy to the surroundings as heat or sound.

faq.q: How can energy efficiency be improved?
faq.a: Reduce friction with lubrication, insulate to reduce heat loss, and choose efficient devices such as LED globes and high star-rated appliances.

items.e: Follow the energy from input to useful output.

items.q: Do a heavy ball and a light ball dropped from the same height land at the same speed (no air resistance)?
c: Yes, because mass cancels in mgh = ½mv².
No, the heavy one is faster.
No, the light one is faster.

items.q: What is mechanical energy?
c: the sum of kinetic and potential energy

items.q: A ball is dropped from 10 m. Ignoring air resistance, how fast is it moving just before it lands? (v = √(2gh))
items.e: mgh = ½mv² → v = √(2 × 9.8 × 10) = 14 m/s. Mass cancels.

items.q: Which energy conversion happens in an LED bulb?
items.e: Follow the energy from input to useful output.

items.q: A device takes in 500 J. Which pair of outputs is possible?
items.e: Outputs must add to the input.

items.q: Which is the efficiency formula?
c: efficiency = useful energy out ÷ total energy in × 100%
items.e: It can also be calculated with power.

A ball falls freely. What happens to its potential and kinetic energy?
c: PE decreases and KE increases by the same amount.

items.q: What does the law of conservation of energy say?
c: Energy is used up over time.
Energy can be created by machines.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed.

c: No, it would have to create energy.

items.e: All the PE (mgh = 2205 J) becomes KE.

items.q: Which energy conversion happens in a wind-up toy?
items.e: Follow the energy from input to useful output.

items.q: Which device converts energy like this: light → chemical?
Snowy 2.0 pumps water uphill when electricity is cheap and releases it later. Why is it not 100% efficient?
c: Some energy is lost as heat and sound in the pumps, pipes and turbines.
items.e: Pumped hydro stores energy as gravitational potential energy.

items.q: Why does oiling a bike chain increase its efficiency?
c: It reduces friction, so less energy is wasted as heat.
items.e: Less friction means more useful output.

items.q: A stone hits the ground at 39.6 m/s after being dropped. Ignoring air resistance, from what height was it dropped? (h = v² ÷ 2g)

Can any real device be 100% efficient?
c: No. Some energy is always transferred as heat to the surroundings.

items.q: What is the main energy input for a coal-fired power station?
items.e: A coal-fired power station: chemical (coal) in → electrical (useful) + heat to the air and water (wasted).

items.q: A 300 kg coaster car is at a point 0 m high on Isla's track. What is its gravitational potential energy there? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Which device converts energy like this: gravitational potential → kinetic → electrical?
Where does the 'wasted' energy in a light bulb go?
c: It goes back into the wall.
It becomes thermal energy in the surroundings.

items.q: What is the main energy input for a solar panel?
items.e: A solar panel: light in → electrical (useful) + heat (wasted).

items.q: What is the useful energy output of a coal-fired power station?
items.e: A coal-fired power station: chemical (coal) in → electrical (useful) + heat to the air and water (wasted).

items.q: What is the main energy input for an LED globe?
items.e: An LED globe: electrical in → light (useful) + heat (wasted).

items.q: How does adding insulation to a ceiling improve a home's energy efficiency?
c: It reduces heat transfer, so less energy is needed for heating and cooling.
items.e: Australian homes get star ratings for energy efficiency.

items.q: What is the useful energy output of an LED globe?
items.e: An LED globe: electrical in → light (useful) + heat (wasted).

items.q: What is the main energy input for a car engine?
items.e: A car engine: chemical (petrol) in → kinetic (useful) + heat and sound (wasted).

items.q: What does a Sankey diagram show?
c: how the input energy splits into useful and wasted energy
items.e: Arrow widths are in proportion to the energy.

items.q: What is the useful energy output of a solar panel?
items.e: A solar panel: light in → electrical (useful) + heat (wasted).

items.q: What is the useful energy output of an electric motor?
items.e: An electric motor: electrical in → kinetic (useful) + heat and sound (wasted).

items.q: What is the useful energy output of an electric kettle?
items.e: An electric kettle: electrical in → thermal energy in the water (useful) + heat to the air and sound (wasted).

items.q: What is efficiency?
c: the percent of input energy that becomes useful output energy

items.q: Why is an LED bulb better than an old incandescent bulb?
c: It converts more of its electrical energy into light.

items.q: A cyclist coasts down a hill and her speed is lower than predicted. Which energy flow was left out of the model?

items.q: Ella's model car rolls down a ramp. At the bottom it has less kinetic energy than the potential energy it had at the top. Where did the rest go?

items.q: A data logger shows a pendulum swing getting lower each time. What does this show?
c: Energy is gradually transferred to the surroundings.
items.e: Air resistance and friction dissipate energy.

items.q: Kai tests insulated and uninsulated cups of hot water. After 20 min, the insulated cup is 15 °C warmer. What does this show?
